title: Automating Coding Workflows with OpenCode 2.0
summary: OpenCode 2.0 provides a framework for developers to integrate autonomous agents into existing CI/CD pipelines.
body_markdown:
## Technical improvements in the OpenCode 2.0 architecture


OpenCode 2.0 introduces a modular architecture that enables you to route complex coding tasks through a unified interface to over 75 different LLM providers.


This design allows the` opencode` command-line interface (CLI) to act as a central traffic controller. It receives instructions from the Web App, Desktop App, or Terminal and passes them to Models.dev, a multi-model aggregation service.


### Using Models.dev as a local gateway


Models.dev is a lightweight binary that functions as a local proxy and router for your AI traffic. You download it as a standalone package or install it via the OpenCode CLI to bridge the gap between your local environment and various model endpoints.


By acting as a local gateway, this tool standardizes the communication between your automation scripts and the diverse APIs of different providers. It handles the translation of request formats and manages the secure storage of your API keys locally.


The illustration of this architecture demonstrates how the CLI abstracts the complexity of different API schemas.


You can swap from a local model to a cloud-based powerhouse without rewriting your automation scripts. This structural flexibility ensures that as new models launch, the underlying workflow remains unchanged.


### OpenCode 2.0's 128k context window


For a developer working on a legacy monolith, this means you can provide context from multiple files at once. The agent understands cross-file dependencies rather than hallucinating functions that don't exist.


Claude Sonnet 5.5 and GPT-6.1 Sol achieve a perfect score of 100 on the[BigCodeBench leaderboard](https://zjshen14.github.io/en/blog/local-qwen-opencode-3090/) .


### Programming language support in OpenCode 2.0


This breadth ensures that teams managing polyglot architectures can use a single agent for systems-level tasks in Rust or Go, data engineering pipelines in Scala or R, and legacy maintenance in COBOL or Fortran.


According to the[OpenCode documentation](https://opencode.ai/v2/docs) , this support is available across the terminal-based interface, the desktop app, and the web app. You can switch from a GUI-based code review to a CLI-based deployment script without losing language-specific linting or logic capabilities.


### OpenCode 2.0's Mixture-of-Experts architecture


The transition to a Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) architecture optimizes performance by activating only a fraction of the total parameters for any given token.


This change reduces the hardware requirements for local hosting. You can run a high-capability model on a single consumer GPU rather than requiring a dedicated server rack.


By routing "expert" sub-networks to handle specific tasks like SQL generation or CSS styling, the model maintains the 73.0 BigCodeBench performance level mentioned by[zjshen14](https://zjshen14.github.io/en/blog/local-qwen-opencode-3090/) .


Furthermore, this significantly lowers latency. For teams scaling across concurrent workflows, this efficiency prevents the compute bottleneck that typically occurs when general-purpose models like Claude Opus 5.5 or Grok 4.7 are hammered with high-frequency, small-scale syntax corrections.
